prerequisites: fundamental learning outcomes for Mathematics I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Defines fundamental concepts related to vectors, matrices, and linear equation systems, and explains the relationships between these structures.

Solves linear equation systems using Gaussian and Gaussian
Jordan elimination methods and interprets the solutions.
Solves algebraic problems using matrix operations, determinant, and inverse matrix concepts.
Analyzes vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, basis, and dimension concepts and applies them to examples.
Relates linear transformations to matrix representations and applies eigenvalue and eigenvector concepts to engineering problems.
Effectively uses linear algebraic methods in modeling and solving problems encountered in engineering and applied sciences.

syllabus_topics: Systems of linear equations and matrix representation
Matrix operations, inverse matrix, and determinant concept
Vector spaces, subspaces, and linear independence
Orthogonal vectors, inner product, Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization process
Fundamental applications of linear algebra in engineering and applied sciences
bibliography: Textbook: D. C. Lay, S. R. Lay, J. J. McDonald, Linear Algebra and Its Applications, Pearson
Reference Books: (1) H. Anton, C. Rorres, A. Kaul, Elementary Linear Algebra with Applications, Wiley
(2) G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, Wellesley-Cambridge Press
